before_snapshot.comment:
APPROVED LITHIUM-FOIL ROLLING ENGINEERING REFERENCE, item31, 2026-10-18. Wickerts corrected SI DOI10.1021/acssuschemeng.4c01782.s001 TableS17 requires lithium-adapted rolling; processing assumptions below are an engineering completion, not reported measurements. Replace the ordinary aluminium-specific rolling service at4.95kgprocessed/kgfinishedLi foil by a dedicated material-neutral mechanical rolling service. Assume0.5kWh electricity perkg rolling throughput, hence2.475kWh perkgfinishedfoil additionally to source2.1kWh generalprocess electricity,4.2MJ cooling and5MJheat retained once. This represents4.95kg cumulative rolling throughput, NOT4.95kg retained lithium or a measured pass count. Assume98percent final lithium retention:1/0.98=1.0204081632653061kg Li from source electrolysis perkgfoil;0.02040816326530612kg process loss. No aluminium feed or aluminium scrap is inherited; ordinary Al rolling elsewhere unchanged. Treat loss through existing hazardous-waste incineration as an explicit reactive-lithium fate proxy; real inert handling/passivation and associated emissions are not modeled. No lithium recovery/secondary-supply credit. Source/reference utilities are engineering proxies; atmosphere/inert gas, lubrication, facility and practical rolling yield/energy remain gaps. Sensitivities90-100percent yield and0.1-1kWh/kg throughput; energy does not scale with yield here because throughput is declared perkgfinishedfoil. No source-specific measured yield is claimed.
PREVIOUS NOTES (retained as history; the correction above takes precedence):
Source: Wickerts et al. (2023). Prospective Life Cycle Assessment of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries for Stationary Energy Storage. ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering. https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.3c00141
before_snapshot.source: Originally from  Wickerts et al. (2023). Prospective Life Cycle Assessment of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries for Stationary Energy Storage. ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering. Based on data and descriptions from Deng et al. (2017), Chordia et al. (2021), Heimes et al. (2018) and Schnell et al. (2018)

CLIC_snapshot.comment:
C100: source-convention internal return of manufacturing offcuts, 1 kg net lithium per kg finished foil, without an external scrap-disposal purchase or recovery credit. The dedicated material-neutral mechanical-energy reference is expanded as 2.475 kWh GLO electricity, separate from retained 2.1 kWh general electricity, 4.2 MJ cooling and 5 MJ heat. The 4.95 coefficient is the source density adjustment, not measured rolling throughput. No aluminium feed/scrap or 98% external-loss/incineration scenario is inherited. Internal handling, remelting, inert atmosphere, lubrication and practical factory coverage remain unquantified. The existing complete-cell factory allocation is retained once; no standalone rolling factory is invented.

Source: Wickerts et al. (2023). Prospective Life Cycle Assessment of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries for Stationary Energy Storage. ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering. https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.3c00141
